chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan narrated from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Do not eat from the game while you are in the state of Ihram, and even if a person in the state of Halal (non-pilgrim) caught it, there is no compensation (fidyah) upon you for what you ate in ignorance, except for the game; for upon you is the compensation for it, whether it was by ignorance or by deliberate action."

key_terms.حَرَامٌ: In the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: One not in the state of Ihram (free from restrictions)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game while in Ihram and is compensation required if done in ignorance?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights a specific juristic distinction in Shia fiqh: while most violations of Ihram prohibitions are excused if committed in ignorance, hunting game incurs fidyah even due to ignorance. This underscores the unique sanctity of the game itself in the sacred precincts, a ruling derived from the principle that the prohibition on game is intrinsic to the state of Ihram rather than merely a restriction on the act of hunting.
